summary: Round 1. NO PRODUCTION LOGIC AND NO TESTS IN THIS DIFF -- five files: a new ADR, an amendment to ADR-0043's Status line, a research revision banner, a field javadoc, and two backlog cells -- so there is no production line to mutate and no assertion to weigh, and I say that rather than inventing a finding. testing.md rules 4-5 have no surface here: no test file is staged, so nothing was weakened. I VERIFIED THE TWO FALSIFIABLE CLAIMS THE DECISION RESTS ON RATHER THAN TAKING THEM. (1) 'NO READER IN THE TREE CONSUMES THEM' IS TRUE. `SubscriptionEvent.byteStart()`/`byteLen()` are called in exactly two places in the tree, both tests (SubscriptionEventGrantTest:66-67, GoldenSubscriptionEventTest:108); no `src/main` file outside `format` reads either. The trap the record names is real and the record is on the right side of it: `SegmentReader.java:138,141` calls `entry.byteStart()`/`entry.byteLen()` on a `RunEntry` -- the segment DIRECTORY's own coordinates, read on every decode -- which is a different field of the same name. (2) THE FIELDS ARE PINNED, NOT MERELY PRESENT, AND THE 'UNPINNED AS WELL AS UNUSED' HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT. I mutated `SubscriptionEvent.decode` to consume both uvarints (so the trailing-bytes refusal still passes) and then force `byteStart = byteLen = RANGE_ABSENT` -- a decoder that silently drops the range -- and ran `:format:test`: 281 tests, 3 RED. GoldenSubscriptionEventTest.aV3DIRECTEventWithARangeMatchesItsGoldenBytes, SubscriptionEventGrantTest.aV3EventSurvivesAROUNDTrip and SubscriptionEventGrantTest.aRangeStartingAtBYTEZEROIsNotMistakenForABSENT all fail, because `equals` enumerates both components (SubscriptionEvent.java:349) and the golden bytes pin the encode side. I restored the file and re-ran the full suite: 1281 tests, 0 failures, tree identical to the staged state. So the fields are a wire contract with no consumer but with real falsifiability, which is exactly what decision (b) needs to be honest about them. THE ARITHMETIC ALSO HOLDS: 2^23 needs 24 bits so 4 uvarint bytes, 5.2 KiB needs 13 bits so 2, plus the presence byte is 7; 7 x 1,600 = 11,200 of 8,388,608 = 0.134%; 7 x 400 = 2,800 = 0.033%. And the four counted facts check out: no `presign` override in either shipping backend, no production `SubscriptionTransport` implementation (only the interface, `ConsumerClient` and `NodeSubscriptions`), exactly one `check-io-seam` exemption (`check-io-seam.sh:58`), and `client/build.gradle.kts` has only `api(project(":format"))`. Both quotes from `check-module.sh` are verbatim (lines 227-234 and 260-262). SIX FINDINGS, FOUR OF THEM BLOCKING, AND ALL SIX ARE ABOUT FALSIFIABILITY RATHER THAN PROSE. Two are criterion 3 unmet -- the sweep's diffable artifact omits the site with the most pattern hits in the corpus, which still states the justification this record calls dead, VERBATIM, in a REVISION BANNER that the corpus README says wins over the body. Two are M5.66's criteria admitting an implementation that constrains nothing, which is the question that row exists to close for the fourth time.

findings.title: the sweep corrects research doc 10 §8 and leaves doc 04 §2c's REVISION BANNER stating the dead justification verbatim -- including the `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))` span this milestone has already established is unreadable
findings.failure_scenario: Criterion 3 asks that every site asserting the coordinates earn their place be corrected or confirmed, with the per-site disposition IN the record. docs/research/30-design-space/04-discovery-and-tailing.md §2c is not in the table at all, and it matches five of the six patterns the record itself names (`byteStart`, `byteLen`, `coordinates`, `M5.44`, `ADR-0043`) with 16 hits -- more than any other research document, and more than doc 10, which IS corrected. It is not a stale body paragraph: it is the CURRENT revision banner, headed 'REVISED 2026-09-11 by M5.14 / ADR-0042' and written in the present tense about what shipped, and docs/research/README.md's rule is that when the body and a banner disagree the BANNER WINS. THREE CLAIMS IN IT ARE WHAT THIS RECORD CALLS DEAD. Line 209-211: '`byteStart` and `byteLen` are on the event again, alongside the grant, because a reader given coordinates can issue ONE request where one without them reads the directory and then the payload' -- that is coalescing-without-a-directory-read, the justification Decision (b) says it replaces rather than repairs. Line 214-215: 'The single request spans `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))` -- header included -- which R7's `h<headerLen>` makes computable in advance' -- M5.45c's cell establishes this exact formula is UNREADABLE (`SegmentReader.open` checks the footer magic before the directory, so the prefix throws 'segment is truncated: no footer magic') and that `[0, objectLen)` is not expressible either. Line 219-221: 'the coordinates let a node union its runs into one ranged GET without reading the directory, which is what "one grant per (node, segment)" needs'. THE RECORD READ THIS SECTION: its own Research header cites 'docs/…/04-discovery-and-tailing.md §2c (the event shape these coordinates come from)'. CONSEQUENCE: the next agent routed to the corpus for 'how does a consumer fetch by coordinates' is told to issue a ranged GET spanning `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))`, in a banner, which is the one thing the whole row exists to kill -- and this is the defect M5.45f's own cell names as 'this milestone's most repeated': a correction applied to one of two places.
findings.suggestion: Give doc 04 §2c the same treatment doc 10 §8 got -- a dated ADR-0044 banner saying the coalescing-without-a-directory-read reason is dead, that `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))` is not readable because the footer magic is checked first, and that the fields are kept for M5.66 -- and add the row to the sweep table with that disposition.

findings.title: the sweep lists GoldenSubscriptionEventTest and omits SubscriptionEventGrantTest, whose class javadoc is the strongest earns-their-place claim in the test tree and ties the fields to a security.md rule 3 half ADR-0043 records as still open and ownerless
findings.failure_scenario: The table's test-tier row is '`format/…/GoldenSubscriptionEventTest`, the six golden files | Unchanged'. The other test file pinning these fields -- format/src/test/java/binjava/format/SubscriptionEventGrantTest.java, 14 pattern hits against GoldenSubscriptionEventTest's 7 -- is absent, and it is the one making a JUSTIFICATION claim rather than a byte claim. Its class javadoc, lines 11-20, reads: 'ADR-0042 then dropped research doc 04 §2c's byteStart/byteLen deliberately and named this row as the one deciding whether closing security.md rule 3's "where possible one range" means bringing them back. It does.' ADR-0043 lines 93-105 already had to correct the neighbouring form of that claim in its own body ('AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS RECORD GOT THAT BACKWARDS. It claimed the coordinates close security.md rule 3's "where possible one range"'), and lines 113-122 conclude 'RULE 3's RANGE HALF IS THEREFORE STILL OPEN … Either way rule 3's range half has no owner.' A reader arriving at the test -- which is where a reader of these two fields lands, since it is the file that constructs them -- is told the rule-3 question was answered by bringing them back, while the two records say it is open. Whether the sentence is false or merely incomplete (it can be read as necessity rather than sufficiency) is exactly what 'corrected or confirmed' is for, and the table answers neither. The same omission covers docs/internal/product/milestones/M5/SPEC.md:301, which matches `coordinates` in FetchPolicyConfig's different sense and would have been a one-line 'Confirmed, different sense' row beside the one already there. The precedent is in the table itself: FetchPolicyConfig.java:19 was named a sweep miss in round 3 of a sibling row and cost a pattern to close.
findings.suggestion: Add SubscriptionEventGrantTest to the table with a real disposition -- either confirm the javadoc (saying it asserts necessity, not that rule 3's range half is closed) or correct the sentence -- and add M5 SPEC.md:301 as 'Confirmed, different sense'.

findings.title: M5.66 criterion 1 cites 'cost.md R12's ~19.5 KiB crossover'; cost.md's R12 is the cost governor, and M5's own SPEC records this exact mis-citation being caught once already
findings.failure_scenario: The criterion reads: 'the crossover is MEASURED … on the `CostTable` prices, given cost.md R12's ~19.5 KiB crossover is derived the same way.' docs/internal/standards/cost.md rule 12 is '**The store is fronted by a cost governor** that refuses, not merely counts' -- no crossover, no derivation, nothing to derive 'the same way' as. cost.md line 10 makes the namespace binding: 'The numbered rules below are the `R<n>` namespace: rule 1 is R1, rule 18 is R18 … renumbering one silently rewrites every citation.' The ~19.5 KiB crossover is R12 of a DIFFERENT numbered table, docs/research/00-problem/02-cost-model.md:299. Whoever takes M5.66 follows the citation to the governor rule and either loses the derivation or, worse, derives the crossover from ratio-to-expected governance. THE TREE HAS ALREADY PAID FOR THIS ONCE, in the same milestone: docs/internal/product/milestones/M5/SPEC.md:301 pins the crossover and ends '⚠️ **not hard-coded**, and ⚠️ **not R12** -- an earlier draft cited it as one, which would have sent a reader to the cost governor.' The new row reintroduces the citation that line exists to forbid, and adds 'cost.md' in front of it, which makes it resolve to the wrong rule rather than merely ambiguous. The same line also carries a fact criterion 1 needs and contradicts: `CostTable` prices REQUESTS only and holds no per-byte transfer price, so a crossover cannot be computed 'on the `CostTable` prices' alone -- the $/GB half is deployment configuration, and M5.11 amended that cell precisely to say so.
findings.suggestion: Cite it as the cost model's R12 with its path (docs/research/00-problem/02-cost-model.md), not as cost.md R12, and say where the per-GB half comes from since `CostTable` does not carry it -- M5 SPEC.md:301 has both corrections already written.

findings.title: M5.66 criterion 2's bounded-read arm is satisfied by a reader that fetches the WHOLE object and slices it in memory, which buys nothing and would then be recorded as the consumer that earns the fields
findings.failure_scenario: Criterion 2's first arm asks for 'a reader that decodes a run from a bounded read, with the codec reachable from what was fetched, AND a consumer that uses the event's coordinates to drive it'. SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION: add `SegmentReader.decodeRun(byte[] wholeSegment, long byteStart, long byteLen)` that opens the whole array exactly as today -- footer magic, directory, everything -- and then slices `[byteStart, byteStart+byteLen)` out of it; have the consumer pass the arriving event's `byteStart`/`byteLen` into it. Every clause is true: a run IS decoded from a bounded read (bounded in the array), the codec IS reachable (the directory was read), and the consumer DOES use the event's coordinates to drive it. The object-store request is byte-for-byte the same whole-object GET, the amplification the row is written about (8 MiB fetched for 5.2 KiB) is unchanged, and criterion 3 then has the javadoc and Decision (b) 'corrected' to say a reader consumes the coordinates -- closing the question a fourth time with a consumer that saves nothing. NOTHING IN THE ROW ASSERTS BYTES FETCHED. Criterion 1 does not backstop it: it asks for the crossover to be measured, not for the implementation to be on the winning side of it, and a measured number in a record constrains no code. This is the shape the neighbouring rows name three times -- 'the seam CAN merge and nothing asks it to' (M5.45c, M5.45h) -- and M5.45h's criterion 1 already had to be rewritten for it ('BOTH HALVES, AND REVIEW MEASURED WHY THE FIRST ALONE IS NOT A CRITERION').
findings.suggestion: Assert the byte count at the seam: 'the fetcher is handed a range and the BYTES REQUESTED are asserted to be O(byteLen) rather than the whole object, at a fixture where the run is a small fraction of the segment' -- otherwise a whole-object fetch followed by an in-memory slice discharges the row.

findings.title: M5.66 criterion 1 says MEASURED but does not say where the number lands, so a paragraph in a commit body discharges it -- the loophole M5.45f's own criterion 3 was rewritten to close
findings.failure_scenario: 'The crossover is MEASURED, not asserted' names no artifact. A sentence in the commit body ('measured at 11% node share') satisfies the wording, and M5.45f's criterion 3 records why that place is wrong: `scripts/review.sh` emits no commit message into either reviewer's packet, so it is invisible at judgement time and sits outside the hash the verdicts bind. A number in an ADR paragraph is better but still static: `CostTable`'s prices can move and nothing goes red, which is the property M5 SPEC.md:301 bought by insisting the threshold be DERIVED from `CostTable.getPerThousand` rather than hard-coded. The row cites that derivation as its model without asking for its mechanism.
findings.suggestion: Say where it lands and what keeps it true: 'the crossover is computed in a case from `CostTable` prices and the configured per-GB rate, so changing either moves it and a hard-coded threshold goes red' -- the M5 SPEC:301 shape.

findings.title: the amendment declares ADR-0043's reopening CLOSED, but the record it points to never mentions security.md rule 3 -- whose range half ADR-0043 hands to M5.45f by name and records as having no owner
findings.failure_scenario: ADR-0043 lines 113-122: 'AND RULE 3's RANGE HALF IS THEREFORE STILL OPEN … whether one ever becomes fillable is M5.45f's to settle. Either way rule 3's range half has **no owner**.' The new Status line says the reopening 'is CLOSED by that record'. ADR-0044 contains no occurrence of 'rule 3' or 'security.md', and M5.66 -- the row created to own what is left -- does not mention it either. So after this commit a reader following ADR-0043's pointer reaches the record named to settle it and finds the question unaddressed, with the tree's only statement on it being 'no owner' in a record now marked amended. It is the weaker sibling of finding t1: not a false claim, a dangling one. The natural home is one sentence -- ADR-0044 settles that no range is expressible, so rule 3's range half is blocked behind M5.66 rather than merely ownerless.
findings.suggestion: One sentence in ADR-0044's Consequences: security.md rule 3's range half is not closable while no range is expressible, so it travels with M5.66; and say so in M5.66's cell so the row that owns the reader owns the rule too.
